trial_title: Gabapentin for Headache in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to see how much gabapentin will reduce headaches associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and to reduce the amount of narcotic pain medication prescribed.

eligibility_table.criterion: Have aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) diagnosed by CT scan of the brain and/or angiogram evidence of intracranial aneurysm (CTA or digital subtraction angiogram or MRA)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has spontaneous intraventricular hemorrhage and arteriovenous malformation (AVM), but there is no mention of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) or evidence of an intracranial aneurysm.
The patient may have a headache due to the head injury and hemorrhage, but it is not explicitly stated whether the headache is symptomatic.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient report a headache intensity of ≥4 on a scale of 0 to 10?

eligibility_table.criterion: Able to swallow and verbalize pain score
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is likely able to swallow and verbalize pain score, as she is conscious and able to communicate.

eligibility_table.criterion: No known allergy to gabapentin or fentanyl
eligibility_table.justification: There is no mention of any known allergies to gabapentin or fentanyl in the patient's profile.
No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a numeric pain score of ≥5 at the time of assessment?

eligibility_table.criterion: Ability to provide written personal consent
eligibility_table.justification: At 32 years old, the patient is likely capable of providing written personal consent.

eligibility_table.criterion: Gabapentin use prior to SAH admission
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is currently on pain medication, but it is unclear if gabapentin was used prior to SAH admission.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient used gabapentin for at least 7 days prior to admission for subarachnoid hemorrhage?

eligibility_table.criterion: Renal failure with creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min
eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: What is the patient's current creatinine clearance value?

eligibility_table.criterion: Unable to receive standard of care pain medications
eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication that the patient is unable to receive standard of care pain medications.
There is no information suggesting that the patient is pregnant or breastfeeding.

eligibility_table.criterion: History of severe depression defined by the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 4th Edition, Text Revision (DSM IV)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's history does not mention severe depression, but there is insufficient information to definitively assess this criterion.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient ever been diagnosed with severe depression as defined by the DSM IV criteria?
